# 1. Introduction
This document contains the evaluation metrics and visual results for the 3D SegResNet model trained on the BraTS 2023 dataset. The metrics were generated by evaluating the model on the unseen test split.

The key metrics computed per region are:
- **Dice Score**: Overlap-based similarity.
- **Hausdorff95 (HD95)**: 95th-percentile surface distance (in mm).
- **Intersection over Union (IoU)**: Jaccard index.
- **Sensitivity**: True positive rate.
- **Specificity**: True negative rate.

The three regions evaluated are **Whole Tumor (WT)**, **Tumor Core (TC)**, and **Enhancing Tumor (ET)**.

# 2. Results Data Processing

First, we load the CSV generated by the `scripts/evaluate_per_patient.py` script.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from pathlib import Path
import os

# Set plotting style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (10, 6)
plt.rcParams['font.size'] = 12

REGIONS = ["Whole Tumor", "Tumor Core", "Enhancing"]

# Construct path relative to this Quarto file
results_dir = Path(".")
csv_path = results_dir / "CSVs" / "test_metrics.csv"
summary_path = results_dir / "CSVs" / "summary_test_metrics.csv"
(results_dir / "figures").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

if csv_path.exists():
    df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
    summary_df = pd.read_csv(summary_path)
    print(f"Successfully loaded {len(df)} patient-region records.")
else:
    print(f"Waiting on {csv_path} to be generated...")
```

# 3. Overall Test Set Performance Summary

The summary table below aggregates the mean and standard deviation of all metrics across the test split.

```{python}
if 'summary_df' in locals():
    # Format the summary dataframe for nice display
    display_df = pd.DataFrame()
    display_df["Region"] = summary_df["Region"]
    
    for metric in ["Dice", "HD95", "IoU", "Sensitivity", "Specificity"]:
        cols = [f"{metric}_Mean", f"{metric}_Std"]
        if all(c in summary_df.columns for c in cols):
             display_df[metric] = summary_df.apply(lambda row: f"{row[cols[0]]:.4f} ± {row[cols[1]]:.4f}", axis=1)
             
    display(display_df)
```

# 4. Statistical Distributions (Box and Violin Plots)

Box plots and violin plots are highly effective for visualising the distribution of metrics across the patient cohort, revealing outliers and the overall consistency of the model.

## 4.1 Dice Score Distribution
```{python}
if 'df' in locals():
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    custom_palette = ["#bfdbf7","#2A9D8F", "#E76F51"]
    ax = sns.violinplot(data=df, x="Region", y="Dice", inner="quartile", hue="Region", palette=custom_palette, legend=False)
    sns.stripplot(data=df, x="Region", y="Dice", color="black", alpha=0.3, jitter=0.2, size=3)
    plt.title("Dice Score Distribution across Test Patients")
    plt.ylabel("Dice Score")
    plt.ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(results_dir / "figures" / "violin_dice.png", dpi=300)
    plt.show()
```

## 4.2 HD95 Distribution
```{python}
if 'df' in locals():
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    custom_palette = ["#bfdbf7", "#2A9D8F", "#E76F51"]
    ax = sns.boxplot(data=df, x="Region", y="HD95", hue="Region", palette=custom_palette, showfliers=False, legend=False)
    sns.stripplot(data=df, x="Region", y="HD95", color="black", alpha=0.3, jitter=0.2, size=3)
    plt.title("HD95 Distance Distribution across Test Patients")
    plt.ylabel("HD95 (mm)")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(results_dir / "figures" / "boxplot_hd95.png", dpi=300)
    plt.show()
```



# 5. Conclusion
The visualizations and tabular statistics generated in this document provide a comprehensive overview of the model's test-time performance. They confirm the distribution characteristics of the predictive segmentations across all test patients, proving to be a solid baseline prior to XAI integration and visualization.
